source.title: Sheaf Discovery with Joint Computation Graph Pruning and Flexible Granularity
source.authors: Lei Yu; Jingcheng Niu; Zining Zhu; Xi Chen; Gerald Penn

page_placements.theme: Attribution graphs and circuits: own-unit circuits vs replacement models with error terms

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether task-specific sheaves made with neuron-level weight pruning and computation-edge pruning preserve model task performance. This is a different method from attribution graphs and does not assess the neuron-explanation claims in the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates task-specific sheaves in GPT-2 and reports performance and sparsity. These results bear on V5's general question of whether model-internal, neuron-level units can preserve behavior, but the paper does not build attribution graphs or test reconstruction error. The other versions are not tested. Results cited from other work, including claims about knowledge neurons, are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A circuit-discovery method paper. It introduces DiscoGP, joint weight and edge pruning in GPT-2 small, and reports that method's fidelity and sparsity against ACDC, EAP, edge pruning and weight pruning. It never builds neuron-based attribution graphs, scores neuron explanations, or audits what neurons do. 'Neuron-level granularity' here means masking individual weight parameters, not treating neurons as explanatory units. Its results are its own method's performance, so it tests no version. The related finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that joint weight-and-edge pruning (DiscoGP) finds sparse, high-fidelity, self-contained sheaves that beat prior circuit-discovery methods. They also report that sheaves can be composed while keeping their function, and that sheaf overlap tracks task similarity. Finally, the sheaves are consistent with a two-stage factual-recall pipeline in GPT-2 small.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based joint pruning of model weights and computation-graph edges to find task-specific sheaves; it does not use the neuron-explanation or attribution-graph procedures named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Task setting changes the reported results; the paper reports results separately across linguistic, IOI, and factual-recall tasks, with an aggregate 93-100% fidelity range in the abstract.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small, jointly pruned subnetworks of the model's own weights and edges (about 0.2–5.7% of weights, 1.7–6.2% of edges) keep 93–100% task accuracy on BLiMP, IOI and PARAREL training sets. They do so under zero ablation, with no trained replacement model. PARAREL test-set accuracy is lower (57.7–95.6%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse subnetworks built from a model's own parameters can reproduce task behaviour in isolation without a replacement model (subnetwork fidelity, not neuron explanation).

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study is limited to GPT-2 base (small) and English tasks. It reports five-run averages but no uncertainty estimates in the provided text. Its evaluation is task performance after pruning, not held-out neuron-explanation prediction or attribution-graph reconstruction.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed task-by-task table values and baseline-method comparisons were not extracted; the abstract's aggregate fidelity result is retained. The paper also reports sparsity and complement accuracy, which do not directly measure V5's stated explanatory claim.

rows.subject: GPT-2 base (small)
rows.operation_detail: Jointly prune computation-graph edges and model weights to produce task-specific sheaves; zero-ablate components outside each sheaf at evaluation.

conditions.value: Across the study's BLiMP, IOI, and PARAREL task settings; aggregate range reported in abstract
five runs per experiment; average performance reported

rows.measure: Sheaf functional fidelity, reported as preserved model performance
rows.baseline: Original model performance; exact baseline values not stated for this aggregate
rows.value: 93-100% of a model’s performance on the identified task
rows.locator: Abstract; §5 and Table 2 for task-level results
rows.note: Aggregate range reported by the paper, not a mean over tasks. The method uses the model's own weights and edges, with no trained replacement model; it is not an attribution-graph evaluation.
rows.check: This row is the study's own method's performance, compared with baselines in Table 2. It measures task accuracy of a pruned weight-and-edge subnetwork under zero ablation. It is not an explanation of behaviour by neuron-level attribution graphs, and not reconstruction error, so it does not measure what V5 names. The 93–100% range is DiscoGP's sheaf accuracy (Table 2: 93.1 to 100). It is not normalized to original-model performance. The PARAREL test-set accuracy is much lower (57.7–95.6%, Tables 11–12).

relation.reason: No version is tested. The paper only discusses neuron-level granularity and prior knowledge-neuron findings, so discusses fits.

tranche.reason: A circuit-discovery method paper on GPT-2 small (joint weight and edge pruning). It neither tests nor uses neuron explanations, neuron audits or neuron-based attribution graphs.

source_check.notes: DiscoGP weight densities in Table 2 are 0.19-2.77%, not up to 5.7%. The PARAREL figures in Table 2 are training-set averages, and test-set accuracy is much lower. The study does not address neuron interpretability and has no verdicts.

statements.correction: Table 2, DiscoGP on GPT-2 small under zero ablation: weight density 0.187-2.77% (0.2-2.8%), edge density 1.68-6.22%, sheaf accuracy 93.1-100%. PARAREL 93.1% is a training-set average over 12 relations. Per-relation PARAREL test-set accuracy is 57.7-95.6% (Appendix D). Per-relation weight density reaches 4.7%. BLiMP and IOI are run on the full datasets. The abstract says 1-7% of the original weights and connections.
statements.problem: The weight range 0.2-5.7% is wrong: 5.71% is the DNA a edge density. DiscoGP weight density tops out at 2.77% in Table 2. The text gives the training-set qualifier only for the PARAREL row; BLiMP and IOI use the full datasets.

reader_labels.reason: The study reports high task fidelity for neuron-level weight-and-edge-pruned sheaves (R1), but tests only GPT-2 base (small), not a large model, and does not evaluate attribution graphs or reconstruction error.
